en.html:
Events were proceeding at a speed which could not be called reasonable.
Not from the beginning, to be fair.

Muramasa came to the detention centre. She had caught Silver Star's presence, she reported. Contact the Kamakura chief of police. Have the release formalities completed. Prisoner Kageaki Minato becomes police auxiliary Kageaki Minato, and walks out of his cell. The man remains the same. The paperwork has improved him.

Then, following Muramasa, to a poor village near Kamakura.
So far, familiar procedure. Nothing unusual worth recording.

The thirty minutes after arrival, however, accommodated several days of what previous cases had required. The clocks here must have faster hands fitted. Some village-specific model.

Five or six metres between us. Staying face-to-face with another warrior at this distance felt persistently wrong.

The proper stage was the sky. Wheeling aerial combat, futawagakari. There, meeting this close was rare. Here we were conducting the whole affair on foot, like two uncles who had brought the world's strongest weapons to settle a parking disagreement.

For him also, presumably, this was unusual. I examined his frame. Type 88 Dragoon, Model A. The 7.7-millimetre machine gun had been removed; senior officers often followed that custom. Standard Yamato Navy tsurugi.

Marines ka aadmi, perhaps? Then his experience of ground fighting should be even less than an army warrior's. That slight sway—measuring my rhythm, certainly. Thodi uncertainty also?

In that case—

The Rokuhara warrior flew.

Off me.
In one instant.
A considerable distance.

One kick from Muramasa's right foot, while he was still sitting on us.

To an observer, at least, that should have been the explanation. Arre, calculate it. Weight of one warrior, downward. Weight of one man underneath, also downward. A leg. Somehow the whole man on top flies away.

Do the arithmetic badly, do it with your eyes closed, put the wrong number on purpose. This result still refuses to arrive.

Magnetism, though, was supplying the missing part. His frame had been magnetised. My kick carried the same polarity. Same polarity repels. With Muramasa's Divine Art doing that preparation, the impossible performance became available.

Receiving gentleman ko samajh aaya? Had the principle reached him along with the foot? No time to ask.

Little damage, I knew. To settle this, the opening had to be used completely. I ran.

Muramasa's magnetic plating lasted briefly by nature. Longer than a second, tremendous caloric consumption. Cancel it, and applying it again required starting from breath regulation.

Begin the fight afresh? Same disadvantage. The neck wound was not shallow. Blood would leave, heat with it.

Abhi. This instant only. There was no spare opportunity kept somewhere for later.

　首筋の傷は浅くはなかった。時と共に血を流し、熱
を失っていくだろう。勝機は今、この刹那だけ。

　是非もなく、戦場はただ一つになる。

　上昇――

He was following the same steps, but unmistakably later. I took the height advantage.

Invert. Descend.

The Type 88 had not even properly begun to climb. Possibly because his departure had been unplanned, he was having enough difficulty merely staying stable.

A sitting duck. A very complete one. I attacked without an answer from him.

No sword. One fist for armament. With that, precisely one vital point was available to destroy.

I approached from behind and punched at his waist.

At her words I examined my condition. Indeed, fighting was not an activity this body could presently offer. The numbness in my fingers was approaching paralysis. The cold through the rest of me was following closely.

I had proposed pursuit without consulting any of the parts that would be doing it. Their objection was becoming unanimous.

Each second made it worse. Remain armoured and flying, and recovery would not come.

Time to withdraw.
